text:
mia (Design): Quick design check-in: new compact scrubber that surfaces sampled-state without taking up the p95 real estate. Prototype: https://redwood.design/ux/compact-scrub-abbrev :link lucy (Frontend): Nice. Can you call out the exact UX goals? Is this mainly to reduce collisions or to educate users about sampling? mia (Design): Both. Goals: 1) avoid overlap in medium-width panels, 2) make sampling provenance obvious, 3) provide a low-friction path to request a full computation. Also we want to A/B the microcopy to see which reduces support tickets. omar (Observability): Perf/infra note: full p95 over long ranges is expensive. We support an async job; client gets job_id + ETA. If UX pushes too many requests we need stronger guardrails. ux-research-bot: Research note: last 50 survey responses show "confused by heatmap" as the top friction for 60% of users who flagged p95 variance. Recommend explanatory copy. rachel (A11y): Accessibility checklist: color-only -> no. Provide tooltip text, keyboard access, and consider pattern overlays for high-contrast. Make sure chip/button contrast meets WCAG 2.1 4.5:1. Also prefer explicit language for screen readers: e.g., aria-label=\"p95 210ms; estimated from sampled traces (ratio 1 to 10)\". lucy (Frontend): Implementation sketch for keyboard: when scrubber is focused, pressing `S` toggles the sampling panel. Panel should trap focus and announce queueing with aria-live. Example snippet: ```

Estimated from sampled traces

Sample ratio: 1:10

``` mia (Design): Microcopy A/B candidates for the chip tooltip (short + long): A1 short chip: "Sampled" A1 tooltip: "Estimated from sampled traces (1 in 10). Request exact computation (async)." B1 short chip: "Estimated" B1 tooltip: "Showing estimates from sampled traces. Click to compute full p95." omar (Observability): I'd prefer Option A for transparency: the word "Sampled" maps well to telemetry. But for support reduction, B's phrase "Showing estimates" might reduce alarm. We can log which variant triggers a compute request and which leads to fewer follow-ups. sam_ops: Backend constraints + telemetry: POST /v1/compute-full-p95 -> {job_id, eta_seconds}. Rate-limit: 25/min per org. We'll emit event `compute_p95.request` and `compute_p95.complete` with tags: range_days, sample_ratio, variant=A|B. Cache full results for 15m. rachel (A11y): Extra note: tooltips should be reachable by keyboard (focusable) and read by screen readers. For the pattern overlay, prefer low-opacity diagonal hatch for low-intensity buckets and crosshatch for medium. Provide an explicit legend entry with text and aria-describedby. lucy (Frontend): Technical perf note: pattern overlays on canvas are heavy. Suggest default color-only heatmap; enable SVG pattern overlay only when `prefers-contrast: high` || userSettings.patterns === true. That limits perf hit. mia (Design): Decision proposal for this sprint: - Chip text: "Sampled" (A1) in UI; tooltip copy use A1 tooltip full sentence - Chip behavior: collapsed icon+abbr under 420px, full text otherwise - Panel: shows sample ratio, selected range, Compute CTA (async) with ETA, and link "Why this is estimated" - Patterns: opt-in via user settings / high contrast only (SVG overlay) - Keyboard: `S` toggles panel when scrubber focused; panel uses aria-live to announce queueing and job completion - A/B: run copy A vs B for 2 weeks and track `compute_p95.request` and support tickets triggered by p95 deltas omar (Observability): I'll add telemetry events and the variant flag. Also will add server-side caching and quota enforcement. sam_ops: I'll draft the API and a short FAQ for support docs explaining ETA variance and costs. rachel (A11y): I'll prepare a quick checklist to validate contrast, keyboard flows, and screen reader messaging once prototype is up. lucy (Frontend): I'll spike the icon-only chip + panel and the SVG pattern toggle. Will measure CPU/paint costs and post results. mia (Design): Great. Please drop prototypes, a11y notes, and the API draft in this thread. I'll file the A/B flag and add copy variations in the branch. Leaving open for small copy edits. :wave:
